chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abul Jarood, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) that he heard him say:
The matter (of leadership/deliverance) is with the youngest of us in age and the most obscure in memory (or reputation).

key_terms.أَصْغَرِنَا سَنًّا: The youngest of us in age

ai.seo_question: Who is the youngest and most obscure among the Imams according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) highlights the principle of 'ghaybah' (occultation) by noting that the Imam will be young and little-known, a detail that aligns with the Twelver Shia belief in the hidden status of Imam al-Mahdi (AJ). It underscores the divine wisdom in concealing the leader's identity to protect him from enemies while maintaining the continuity of spiritual authority during the period of waiting.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (1) Ali bin Ahmad narrated from Obaydillah bin Musa from Muhammad bin al-Husayn (from) ibn Abul Khattab from Muhammad bin Sinan from Abul Jarood that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) had said:

“This matter (deliverance) will be carried out by the youngest and obscurest one of us.” The same was narrated by Ali bin al-Husayn from Muhammad bin Yahya al-Attar from Muhammad bin Hassaan ar-Razi from Muhammad bin Ali as-Sayrafi from Muhammad bin Sinan from Abul Jarood from Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as).
